notes.claim: In OpenStax Precalculus, the terminal side of an angle meets the unit circle at the point (x, y), which is equivalent to (cos t, sin t).
Sine, cosine and tangent take positive or negative values depending on the quadrant the angle is in.
A reported student error is taking the x-coordinate on the unit circle as the sine ratio, when the unit circle gives cosine as x and sine as y.

sources.title: 5.2 Unit Circle: Sine and Cosine Functions - Precalculus 2e | OpenStax
sources.quote: The terminal side of the angle intersects the circle at the point (x,y), which is equivalent to (cos t, sin t).

sources.title: Trigonometric skills - National 5 Maths - BBC Bitesize
sources.quote: Sine, cosine and tangent all have different positive or negative values depending on what quadrant they are in.
